Christian Mensah’s knowledge changes because of what his investigation uncovers.

At the end of Scenario 3, Christian only believes that Jonathan’s trouble may be related to criminal activity. Jonathan tells him he “might have gotten involved with the wrong people” but denies doing anything illegal himself. Christian does **not** yet know that Jonathan is being framed, nor does he know who the real culprit is. He only decides to investigate discreetly.

In Scenario 4, Christian’s investigation provides new information: he learns that Jonathan is being framed. Christian then tells Jonathan, “I believe you’re being framed. Someone is trying to set you up.” This is the new belief that replaces his earlier suspicion of possible criminal involvement. At this point, he still does not know exactly who is responsible; he only has leads.

So the belief change from Scenario 3 to Scenario 4 is caused by further investigation showing that Jonathan is being framed, not by Christian’s prior worry, intention to help, or later sense of betrayal.
